title: Creating Certificate Signing Requests for Enrollment (CA) Certificates

blocks.text: A CA certificate is required for enrolling Zscaler Client Connector, when configuring an App Connector for enrollment, and when configuring an AppProtection-enabled application segment for enrollment.

Zscaler recommends creating a CA certificate for Zscaler Client Connector and another certificate for App Connectors. If you have AppProtection enabled, you need to create an additional CA certificate.
To create a certificate signing request (CSR) for an enrollment (CA) certificate:

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Private Access > Private Infrastructure > Enrollment Certificates.
Name: Enter a name for the CSR. The name cannot contain special characters, with the exception of periods (.), hyphens (-), and underscores ( _ ).

You cannot create a CSR with a canonical name (CNAME) that is a duplicate to a CNAME of another CSR. If the name of the CSR is updated, the CNAME remains the same. For example, if you create a CSR with the name test, the CNAME for the certificate is {domain}/test. If you rename this certificate to test1, the CNAME will not change (i.e., {domain}/test). If you try to create a new CSR with the name test, then the CNAME for the new certificate is {domain}/test, and the CNAME doesn't change.
Store in HSM: Select True to store both the public and private keys for the generated CSR in a hardware security module (HSM) for additional protection.
Click Create to generate content for the CSR.
Sign the CSR using your organization's signing CA, which can be a root or intermediate CA. This will result in the CSR becoming a signed certificate.

blocks.text: The Enrollment Certificates page automatically updates to display your pending CSR in the table, where you must upload the signed certificate and the certificate chain.
